t: You're at the Wiener Holocaust Library, in Russell Square. It's the world's oldest institution devoted to the study of the Holocaust, its causes and legacies. It was founded in 1933 as an information bureau, telling Jewish communities and governments worldwide about the Nazi persecution of the Jews. After the Second World War it became a research institute and public library. It takes its name from Alfred Wiener, a German Jew who spent much of his life documenting antisemitism and racism, and who directed the library for many years.
